chapter: Blue Devils, Moten and the Reno Club
title: The vacant-lot radio story Basie did not tell
summary: Kuehl reads a quote about Goodman tuning in the Reno Club broadcast from a vacant lot; Basie dismisses it as invented by the writer.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Sweets told me that you were an old
buddy of Clarence Holiday's in the band.
Yes. Sweets? What did he know about it?
That's all he told me.
Where did you interview him at?
In Los Angeles, five years ago.

Okay. Let's see. "We were broadcasting over a local Kansas City station from the Reno Club and John told Benny to listen in on one of the broadcasts." All right. "Benny did and he was interested enough to make a special trip to Kansas City to hear the band in person." Is that when you met him?
Met who?
Benny Goodman.
No.
He didn't come?
I guess somebody said he was there.

Oh, I see. I see. "I might add that Benny's own band was playing in Chicago at the time and as he later told me, the only way he could pick up the station on which we were broadcasting was by going out into the middle of a vacant lot with a portable radio." Is that so?
He told me that?
Did he?
That's what Benny said?
This is what you said.
Oh, that's full of shit. (Inaudible) that I don't remember.
I've never been talking about that at all. I don't know. I don't know where these people get these things. Now, this man's just writing a story.
But you see, the thing is, when I read this book, I believed that that's what you're saying.
Well, that's what you're supposed to.
Right, exactly.
Yeah.
Strange business.
No, he's building a thing and Benny probably did say that to somebody.
(Laughter.)
That could be very possible, you know?
